correctness.rationale: For generic central planes, crossed edges count section vertices exactly: two base-edge intersections on each cap until the extremal vertex projection, and two vertical-edge intersections per antipodal pair below the threshold. The exact Haar distribution of h|U_z|/sqrt(1-U_z^2) gives the order-statistic integral law. For m>=3 its quadrilateral contribution is unique, with strict pointwise monotonicity and dominated limits. For regular hexagons, direct arcsine antiderivatives, algebraic inversion, and the single-root derivative test at x=2/3 give the exact formulas and sharp optimizer. An executable compared independent edge counts, law integrals and frequencies in 15 parameter configurations; these finite checks are auxiliary.

originality.rationale: A literature-led comparison found no supported implication of the universal order-statistic central-section law or height-rigidity and sharp regular-hexagon optimum. Full texts of the two highly relevant classical stereology papers were unavailable, so historical priority is provisional; different random-offset ensembles do not automatically give conditional Haar central laws.
residual_risks: Complete full texts of Voss (1982) and Ohser–Mücklich (1995) were not accessible, so possible hidden stronger statements or tables have not been excluded.
A classical stereology text may have derived equivalent central-normal conditional laws under different terminology; historical originality is provisional.

value.rationale: A complete classification of possible generic central-section side counts and their exact probabilities for every fixed centrally symmetric polygonal base is a natural stereological shape-inference result. The strictly monotone quadrilateral frequency identifies the height of every such right prism when the base is known. The canonical regular hexagonal prism supplies a fully elementary 4/6/8 distribution and a unique nontrivial maximum of the octagon frequency; these are precise reusable geometric invariants rather than arbitrary numerical slices.
